entities.summary: Theudebald, Duke of Alamannia (730-746 CE), played a pivotal role in shaping the medieval region of Alamannia. Born into a powerful family, Theudebald rose to prominence as the Duke of Alamannia, succeeding his brother Lantfrid. He ruled alongside Lantfrid until 730, when Lantfrid's deposition led to Theudebald's ascension to the throne. Theudebald's leadership was marked by a series of military campaigns against the Franks and the Lombards, ultimately securing a fragile peace in the region. His reign also saw the establishment of trade routes and the growth of cities, transforming Alamannia into a hub of cultural and economic exchange. Theudebald's legacy was cemented by his efforts to promote Christianity and establish a strong sense of identity among his people. As the last Duke of Alamannia, he left an indelible mark on the region's history, shaping its future for generations to come.
